name: Protective town of San Miguel and the Sanctuary of Jesús Nazareno de Atotonilco
description: In the highlands of central Mexico, San Miguel de Allende is a former fortified town founded in the 16th century to guard the Royal Route inland. Its churches and civic buildings are mostly 18th-century Mexican Baroque. Fourteen kilometres away, the Atotonilco sanctuary has a church and chapels covered in painted murals, which have earned it the nickname "Sistine Chapel of Mexico.
